description: Two checks that no schema can ever make, because the parser has already destroyed the evidence by the time a schema sees the instance. Both wrappers implement them independently — the Python leg through a parse hook, the Node leg by scanning the raw text — and are contracted to emit the same lines in the same order.

cases.name: without the flag a duplicate member is invisible and the last value wins
cases.description: Without the flag, last-value-wins parsing hides the duplicate entirely, and a const on the last value passes.

cases.name: with the flag a duplicate member is a verdict about the document
cases.description: With the flag, the duplicate is a verdict about the submitted document.

stdout: INVALID: instance contains duplicate member name "status"

cases.name: duplicate names are deduplicated and sorted, so both legs agree word for word
cases.description: All duplicate names are reported, deduplicated and sorted, so the two legs agree word for word despite visiting objects in different orders.

stdout: INVALID: instance contains duplicate member name "a"
INVALID: instance contains duplicate member name "b"

cases.name: a duplicate at any depth counts

stdout: INVALID: instance contains duplicate member name "x"

cases.name: a non-ASCII duplicate name prints identically on both legs
cases.description: A non-ASCII name must print byte-identically on both legs.

stdout: INVALID: instance contains duplicate member name "café"

cases.name: an escaped name and its literal form are the same member
cases.description: Escape sequences are decoded before comparison, so \u0061 and a are the same member.

stdout: INVALID: instance contains duplicate member name "a"

stdout: INVALID: instance contains duplicate member name "id"
